checks.title: Firmware is up to date
checks.check: Do this first. In Manager, press the vertical "..." and select About to see your firmware and Manager versions. Compare your firmware with the latest XIM MATRIX release at xim.tech/downloads.

why.text: XIM updates the MATRIX firmware often, with new features and fixes. Even a brand-new MATRIX can have old firmware. XIM's troubleshooting pages say to update first, before you troubleshoot anything else.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX is frequently being updated with new features and fixes. It is recommended that you upgrade if there is an update available before continuing troubleshooting.

Even a new XIM MATRIX may have firmware that is out of date.
To access versioning, press the vertical "..." and select About.
Please make sure you are running our latest firmware which will have all our most recent fixes.

fix.text: Update with the XIM MATRIX Firmware Flash Tool from xim.tech/downloads. You need a Windows PC or a Mac and a USB connection. Start with the MATRIX unplugged. Hold the button on the MATRIX while you plug it into the computer: it lights blue, which means it is ready to flash. Back up your MATRIX, then press Update Firmware and wait for the rainbow startup sequence. If the update fails on a PC, XIM suggests rebooting, trying another USB port or cable, and disabling extra anti-virus software.

citations.quote: Navigate to xim.tech/downloads, select XIM MATRIX and you’ll be directed to our community forum where all our firmware releases are stored.

Press the Update Firmware button to update your XIM MATRIX.

checks.title: Your Config is for Destiny 2 and its Smart Translator is current
checks.check: Open Manager's dashboard. Check that the current Config shows Destiny 2 and the platform that matches your output. On Xbox, that is Xbox. On PC, it is PC if you output as an XInput controller (including Mouse, Keyboard, Controller), Xbox if you output as an Xbox controller, or PlayStation 5 if you output as a DualSense. On PC, also check that the Config's output is a controller: Controller (PC XInput) or Controller (Xbox, PS, PC). Mouse, Keyboard, Controller also aims through the controller, but Dialed doesn't cover it yet. A mouse-and-keyboard output Config has no Smart Translator. Then look for a warning exclamation icon: it means the Config's Smart Translator is out of date.

why.text: Every controller-output Config has a Smart Translator: XIM's per-game aim system that handles reticle speed for you. A game's Smart Translator can be updated when the game's aiming system changes, and Manager warns you when yours is out of date. XIM's cm/360 checklist asks for the Config that matches your game and a translator that isn't out of date.

checks.title: The DPI in your Config matches your mouse
checks.check: Enter your mouse's DPI in your Config. Then run Check DPI: in Manager, press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds and select Check DPI. Put a ruler (or a ruler app) under the mouse and move it 1 inch sideways. The value shown should be close to your DPI. Keep the mouse still to reset.

why.text: Real-world sensitivity (cm/360) is only accurate if the DPI in your Config matches your mouse. If the DPI is wrong, your aim won't be accurate. Gaming mice don't always make it clear whether a setting really saved to the mouse, and the MATRIX has tools to check the true DPI and polling rate.

citations.quote: Your mouse DPI (dots-per-inch) is a very important value that is set in your Config. If it is wrong, your mouse aim won't be accurate.
Accurate real world units require your mouse DPI be set correctly in your Config. Make sure this value matches your mouse DPI.
Gaming mice can be complex devices where it's not always clear if settings are saved on-device. XIM MATRIX provides tools to check the true DPI and polling rate of your mouse.

fix.text: The value doesn't have to match exactly, but it should be in range. If it isn't, make sure your DPI setting is really saving to your mouse, then test again.

citations.quote: Gaming mice use high resolution sensors, it's normal to not match your DPI exactly, but, it should be within the range. If it's not, verify that your DPI selection is saving correctly to your mouse.

checks.title: Your mouse reaches its polling rate
checks.check: Run Check Rate: in Manager, press and hold the mouse icon for 3 seconds, select Check Rate, and move the mouse in continuous circles. The value shown should be close to the polling rate you set. Also look up your mouse on XIM's Hardware Compatibility List: some mice are listed as not working, or as usable only at a lower polling rate.

why.text: Your mouse may not actually run at the polling rate you set, because of its onboard memory settings or wireless interference. Check Rate counts how many movement reports the MATRIX really gets from your mouse each second. XIM's cm/360 checklist asks for a correct response rate: the rate Check Rate shows (not the Response smoothing setting).

citations.quote: Your mouse may not respond at the polling rate you set due to onboard memory setting issues or wireless interference.
The response rate tool is measuring the count of non-zero values coming from your mouse every second.

fix.text: If the value isn't close to your polling rate, make sure your polling rate is really saving to your mouse. If the Hardware Compatibility List marks your mouse as usable only at a lower polling rate, use that rate.

checks.title: Light notifications are on, and you know what they mean
checks.check: Edit your Config, press "..." in the Identity section, and make sure the light aim speed and mode notifications are not disabled. Then learn the signals. Rapid purple blinking at random times: timing errors. A quick red flash: you hit the game's maximum turn speed. A quick green flash: the MATRIX saw you aim down sights (ADS). A quick yellow flash: you went back to hip fire. Repeated yellow blinking is different: it means the MATRIX lost contact with the authentication controller in Port 3 (see the authentication controller check for Xbox, or for Xbox and DualSense output on PC). If the light is hard to see, you can adjust its brightness in Global Settings.

why.text: The MATRIX's light tells you what it is doing. Rapid purple blinking means timing errors that may hurt performance. With controller output, every console shooter has a maximum turn speed, and the MATRIX flashes red when you hit it. The green and yellow flashes tell you your Config's game roles are set up right, so the MATRIX knows when you aim down sights.

citations.quote: Your XIM MATRIX's light is used to let you know about it's current state of operation which is covered throughout the rest of this guide.
Disabling light aim speed and mode light notifications
Rapid purple blinking: If your XIM MATRIX is blinking like this at seemingly random times, it means there are timing errors detected that may result in non-optimal performance.

If you are gaming with controller output, then, you need to be aware of the game's maximum turn speed limit. All console shooters have different limits and your XIM MATRIX will notify you when you hit that limit by quickly flashing red so you can adjust accordingly.

Your XIM MATRIX will notify you whenever you switch between Hip and Aim Down Sight (if your game is configured for both modes). This is done so that you can know that your Config's game roles are set up correctly.
When you enter Aim Down Sight, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash green.
When you return to Hip, your XIM MATRIX will quickly flash yellow.
Your XIM MATRIX needs to know when your game is firing and when it's in aiming down sight (ADS) mode in order to function correctly.
Repeated yellow blinking: Your XIM MATRIX has lost communication with your authentication controller.
You can also disable your XIM MATRIX light breathing animations and adjust the light's brightness.

fix.text: Purple blinking: check for loose USB connections, faulty cables and hubs. No green flash when you aim down sights: open Game Roles (press "..." and select Game Roles) and set ADS to the button Destiny 2 uses for it. If ADS is on a trigger, also check how far it must be pulled to count (Trigger Roles). XIM says to keep it at 1% if you are unsure. Red flashes: you are turning as fast as the game allows, and no setting can go past the game's limit.

citations.quote: Check for loose USB connections, faulty cables, hubs, or other hardware.
To access, press the "..." and select Game Roles.
To change, select one and choose a different button that activates the mode in your game.
You can specify how far the trigger must be pulled for the game to fire or enter ADS.
If you are unsure, simply keep the values at 1%.
This is because no matter what, you cannot exceed the turn speed restrictions built into the game.

checks.title: Test sensitivity under clean conditions
checks.check: Before you judge your sensitivity, remove anything that changes real-world cm/360, just for the test: use the linear (default) aiming curve and disable quantization. On Xbox with an Elite 2 controller, make sure no controller stick curve is on. Check that the "cm/360" label in your Config isn't red. Test in a training area or private match with no enemies, so aim assist can't slow your reticle. XIM's test: set 40 cm/360, then move the mouse 10 cm sideways at a moderate speed. You should turn a quarter turn (90 degrees), for example from one wall of a room to the next.

why.text: XIM defines accurate cm/360 as your mouse movement physically matching your sensitivity setting when you use a linear (default) aiming curve. XIM's cm/360 checklist says to test with a linear curve, quantization off and, on Xbox, no Elite 2 stick curve. XIM also warns that quantization may hurt real-world sensitivity accuracy. A red "cm/360" label means your Config doesn't support accurate cm/360. XIM says accurate cm/360 isn't strictly necessary, but it is required for consistent sensitivity between Configs.

citations.quote: An accurate cm/360 means that your mouse behavior physically matches your sensitivity setting when using a linear (default) aim response curve.
You are testing with a linear aiming curve (not a custom one)
You have quantization disabled
If using an Elite 2 on Xbox, make sure you don't have a controller stick curve enabled
Applying quantization to your mouse or motion aim may negatively affect real world sensitivity accuracy.
Your Config supports it (you will see the "cm/360" label display in red if it doesn't).
Make sure your in-game environment isn't artificially slowing your reticle (aim assist)
Although an accurate cm/360 isn't strictly necessary to be able to use and enjoy you XIM MATRIX, it is required if you want
Consistent sensitivity between your Configs
Set your mouse sensitivity to 40 cm/360
citations.note: XIM's test, used in the check.

citations.quote: Start your game in a training area or private match (without enemies that can cause aim assist slowdown)
Move your mouse at a moderate speed horizontally 10 centimeters (which is a quarter turn, 90-degrees)
citations.note: XIM's test, used in the check.

why.caveat: Dialed makes one config sheet per loadout, one Config each, so consistent sensitivity between Configs matters here.

fix.text: Switch these off only for the test, then put back what you use. They are features, not faults: XIM offers quantization to improve compatibility with aim assist, and custom curves let you shape your aim any way you like. If your result is way off (it doesn't need to be exact), recheck your DPI, your mouse's rate (Check Rate), Config, Smart Translator and in-game settings, then test again. If the cm/360 label is red, your Config doesn't support accurate cm/360 yet. Let XIM staff know: XIM says updating that Smart Translator will then be prioritized.

citations.quote: I recommend to use 1000Hz, because that will give you the most responsive mouse movements.
citations.note: Same script. A general recommendation, not tied to Overwatch 2. The script's separate "feel like a xim Apex" section also sets 1000Hz; Dialed does not use that section.

statements.caveat: From a 2023 tutorial, so Manager's menus may have changed. The current guide places an update rate in the Config's output connection mode, with Standard as the default, and gives no Hz values. We can't confirm that XIM Central's "polling rate" is the same setting, or what Standard equals. If a game needs SAB, follow the guide and keep Standard.
